uncited: *   **Input:** Global voxel dataset of size $V$ samples; number of processing nodes $N$; macro size $M$ (number of voxels per macro).
The dataset is partitioned into macros of fixed size $M$.
Each macro is assigned to a specific node.
The classification depends on the spatial relationship between macros assigned to the same node.
**Partition:** Divide the global voxel array into non-overlapping macros of size $M$.
*   Let $S_i$ be the set of spatial indices of voxels contained in macros assigned to node $i$.
*   **Grouped Condition:** The union of spatial indices in $S_i$ forms a contiguous sub-volume.
*   **Interleaved Condition:** The spatial indices in $S_i$ are scattered or non-contiguous.
*   **Boundary Fetches:** Resampling requires data at neighboring points.
*   **Time Complexity:** Communication cost depends on the distribution.
Interleaved distributions do not require replication but may have higher communication latency.
Interleaved distributions may offer better load balancing if the workload is uneven.
*   **When to Use:** Use Grouped for cache-sensitive applications with uniform data.
Use Interleaved for load-balanced scenarios where communication latency is less critical than compute balance.
It addresses the fundamental trade-off between spatial locality (cache performance) and load balancing in parallel volume rendering.
